item.title: Fixing Date/Time Parsing Issues: Format M vs m and Year 'u' vs 'y'
item.description:
“Fixing Date/Time Parsing Issues: Format M vs m and Year ‘u’ vs ‘y’”

When working with date and time manipulation in modern Java or Kotlin, correctly specifying the pattern in DateTimeFormatter is critical. Several common pitfalls involve confusing month and minute placeholders, or selecting the appropriate year representation. How does one correctly handle parsing ISO standard date-time strings and formatting them while avoiding common pattern mismatches?

Why Does My Date/Time String Parse Without an Explicit Formatter?

For an input string conforming precisely to the ISO 8601 standard, such as "2006-03-25T10:30:00+12:00", the default parsing mechanism, specifically OffsetDateTime#parse(), often succeeds without supplying an explicit DateTimeFormatter.
